 SM Classics takes K-pop orchestras beyond Asia
 by Joonha Yoo 
 Posted : November 17, 2026, 17:59 
 Updated : November 17, 2026, 17:59 
 Share 
 Print 
 A+ 
 A- 
 Close share menu 
 Girls' Generation's Yuri serves as moderator during the "SM CLASSICS LIVE in TAIPEI" orchestral concert at the National Concert Hall in Taipei on Nov. 14–15, 2026. Courtesy of SM Entertainment 
SEOUL, November 17 (AJP) - SM Entertainment's classical music label SM Classics has completed four orchestral concerts in Hanoi and Taipei, including a sold-out show in Vietnam, as it prepares to expand its K-pop concert series to Hong Kong and Canada next year, the company said Tuesday.
The "SM CLASSICS LIVE" series reimagines songs by SM artists as classical and orchestral performances, bringing familiar K-pop melodies to international concert halls.
The Hanoi concert took place at Ho Guom Opera House on Nov. 5 as part of the Korean government's 2026 Korea Season cultural exchange program. Conductor Yuwon Kim led the Vietnam National Symphony Orchestra, joined by Super Junior's Ryeowook and violinist Jung Hyun-jun.
The program included orchestral arrangements of NCT Dream's "Never Goodbye" and EXO-K's "MAMA," alongside Korean and Vietnamese folk songs.
 A panoramic view of the "SM CLASSICS LIVE in TAIPEI" orchestral concert at the National Concert Hall in Taipei on Nov. 14–15, 2026, featuring classical arrangements of SM Entertainment's K-pop hits. Courtesy of SM Entertainment 
The tour continued with three performances at Taipei's National Concert Hall on Nov. 14 and 15, featuring Taiwan's National Symphony Orchestra under conductor Thanapol Setabrahmana.
Girls' Generation's Yuri hosted the Taipei concerts, while Ryeowook appeared as a soloist at all four performances across the two cities. The Taipei program featured orchestral interpretations of TVXQ!'s "Rising Sun," Taeyeon's "U R" and Red Velvet's "Psycho."
SM Classics will next perform at the 55th Hong Kong Arts Festival from March 12 to 14, 2027, followed by two concerts at Toronto's Roy Thomson Hall on June 29 and 30.
The Hong Kong performances will feature Ryeowook and Red Velvet's Wendy, while Wendy will also join the Toronto Symphony Orchestra for the Canadian concerts.
The upcoming shows extend a tour that has already visited Seoul, Tokyo, Vienna, Singapore and Bangkok, as SM seeks to bring its K-pop catalog to audiences through classical music. 
 Joonha Yoo 
 Joonha Yoo is a bilingual journalist at AJU Press (AJP), covering music, culture, entertainment and Korea’s automotive industry. 
Raised in Fort Collins, Colorado, he often writes from the scene, bringing firsthand detail to stories ranging 
from BTS comeback concerts to unique cultural events that catch the world's eye.

 SM Entertainment hit by data breach 
 Captured photo of SM Entertainment's official webpage showcasing the official apology letter regarding the data breach took place NOV 4. SEOUL, November 09 (AJP) - SM Entertainment and two of its affiliates have suffered a data breach exposing sensitive personal information, including national identification numbers, bank account details and contract records. The company said an external attacker gained unauthorized access to internal business systems, including its electronic document approval platform, and extracted stored files around Nov. 4. The compromised information includes names, phone numbers, addresses, South Korean resident registration numbers, bank account details, job titles and information contained in contracts. The breach also affected DearU, operator of the fan communication platform Bubble, and concert production company Dreammaker Entertainment. DearU said the exposed records concerned employees and that Bubble users' personal information was not affected. SM said it immediately blocked the IP addresses and access routes used in the attack and replaced compromised access keys. It is investigating the incident with relevant authorities and outside security specialists. LED screen in front of the HQ SM Entertainment show images of various SM artists throughout the day. AJP Yoo Na-hyun The company has not disclosed how many people were affected or how many documents were taken. It said it was identifying affected individuals and notifying them by email or text message. No secondary damage has been confirmed so far, SM said, but the company warned of possible phishing attempts and fraudulent calls impersonating its representatives. SM apologized for the breach and pledged to strengthen its internal security controls and monitoring systems. 
 SM Entertainment Seeks Recovery After Weak Third Quarter Performance 
 SM Entertainment reported a disappointing performance for the third quarter of this year, attributed to a decrease in domestic album activities by its artists. The company plans to rebound in the fourth quarter and the first quarter of next year with a strong lineup of new releases and large-scale global tours.On November 4, SM announced that its consolidated revenue for the third quarter reached 291.1 billion won, with an operating profit of 35.5 billion won. These figures represent declines of 9.5% and 26.4%, respectively, compared to the same period last year. The net profit turned to a loss due to foreign exchange losses stemming from the strengthening of the won.On a separate basis, the company reported revenue of 173.4 billion won (down 22.8% year-on-year), operating profit of 28.4 billion won (down 29.2%), and net profit of 11.1 billion won (down 65.7%). SM explained, "To strengthen our global fandom, we strategically conducted overseas and small-scale performances, which led to a relative decrease in domestic album activities, resulting in declines in album, digital music, and concert revenues, as well as operating profits from some subsidiaries."In contrast, the advertising and event segments, along with the merchandise and licensing sectors, showed positive results. Revenue from planned merchandise sales and IP collaborations increased by 21.3% and 23.5%, respectively, reaching 29.2 billion won and 62.1 billion won compared to the previous year. Among subsidiaries, Dear U recorded an operating profit of 9.2 billion won (+5.6%), continuing its growth, while Dream Maker and KeyEast successfully turned a profit. However, SM C&C and SM Life Design Group saw a decline in profitability.SM aims to recover its growth trajectory in the fourth quarter and the first quarter of next year by launching a diverse lineup of artists. In the fourth quarter, following the releases of NCT WISH and RIIZE, new albums from NCT DREAM and Taeyeon, a mini-album from the EXO unit (Kai & Sehun), and a Japanese single from Yunho will be released. In the first quarter of next year, new albums from RIIZE, Jaehyun, and Seulgi, along with a mini-album from Hearts2Hearts, a group single from Super Junior-83, and a Japanese single from NCT JNJM will be unveiled.The scale of global concerts will also be significantly expanded. NCT WISH, which sold out its first solo concert at Gocheok Sky Dome, and aespa, which successfully completed its North American tour, will embark on a European tour covering nine cities, including Paris and London. Additionally, major artists will actively perform worldwide, including NCT 127's fifth tour, EXO's encore concert, WayV's China tour, and solo tours by Changmin, Minho, and Yesung.SM stated, "Starting early next year, we will continue the growth momentum through new releases and global activities of our major artists, while also expanding the activities of legacy artists and entering new markets with younger artists to build a balanced IP portfolio."* This article has been translated by AI. 
 SM Group's SM Credit Information Receives ESG Certification from Red Cross 
 SM Group's manufacturing and service subsidiary, SM Credit Information, has received certification as an ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) practicing company from the Korean Red Cross.On the 26th, SM Credit Information held a certification ceremony at its headquarters in Yeongdeungpo, Seoul, where CEO Gong Mun-yong and Kim In-sook, head of the Red Cross's Sharing Planning Team, along with key executives from both organizations, expressed their commitment to ongoing charitable activities and collaboration.The Red Cross's ESG practicing company program awards certification to businesses that contribute to society and create public value through regular monthly donations and other initiatives. SM Credit Information aims to enhance its capabilities in social contribution, reflecting the emphasis placed by SM Group Chairman Woo Oh-hyun on coexistence and mutual growth as a key management priority.Funds raised through SM Credit Information's regular donations will be prioritized for families in crisis and neighbors in welfare blind spots who have not received adequate support. Both organizations are committed to providing tailored welfare services that go beyond basic livelihood support, including emotional care, medical expense assistance, and improvements to living conditions.CEO Gong stated, "The Red Cross's regular donations represent a concrete example of the company's pursuit of social responsibility, as it goes beyond simple charity to share warmth and communicate with the community. We will continue to plan and operate various ESG programs to ensure that the positive impact of these efforts reaches more neighbors in need."Founded in 1999, SM Credit Information specializes in debt collection, credit investigation, and asset management services. It became part of SM Group in December 2015.* This article has been translated by AI.
